sources.entry: Pulse - Native app that shows how much Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and 70+ other AI coding services you have left, as rings docked at the edge of your screen. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/qunqin24/Pulse) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Pulse is a free, open-source, native macOS app that shows remaining usage for many AI coding services (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and more) as rings docked at the edge of the screen.
summary.what_it_does: Pulse displays a ring for each monitored AI coding service showing how much of its usage limit is used or left, with the percentage taken from what the service itself reports. Hovering a ring opens a card with every limit, its reset time, the plan, and recent usage from local records. It includes a burn-rate forecast that estimates when your pace will run out before the window resets. The app can dock on any screen edge, fold to a sliver when idle, or show usage in the menu bar. It also tracks local token spend priced at public API rates, shows status pages for 44 providers with outage notifications, and offers usage recap cards. According to the README, it reads credentials from logins the user already has and sends nothing to a Pulse server.
use_cases: check remaining Claude Code or Codex usage
avoid surprise AI coding rate limits
monitor Cursor and GitHub Copilot quotas
track AI coding token spend by model
get notified when a usage limit is nearly reached
how_to_run: Download the latest Pulse-x.y.z.dmg from Releases and drag Pulse into Applications
On first launch, choose the services to monitor and click Done
If blocked by Gatekeeper, open System Settings > Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway, or run: xattr -cr /Applications/Pulse.app
Build from source: git clone the repository, cd Pulse, then run ./Scripts/bundle.sh
Launch the built app with: open build.noindex/Pulse.app
notable: Covers 76 AI coding services, each read through its own usage endpoint, editor login, local language server, or pasted key
Burn-rate forecast predicts when usage will run out before the window resets
Docks along any screen edge beside the Dock or folds to a sliver; also available in the menu bar
No Pulse account or server; keys are stored encrypted on the user's Mac
Provides a Pulse --json command-line option for scripts
caveats: Requires macOS 14 Sonoma or newer; building current sources needs full Xcode and the macOS 26 SDK
Not signed with an Apple Developer certificate, so first launch requires a Gatekeeper workaround
Some figures are estimates, and services that report no usage show nothing rather than a guess
